themes_detail.label: Residential Waste Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints spiked to 8 complaints THIS WEEK, a 191% increase over the 2.8 weekly average from the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a sudden waste management or illegal dumping problem emerging in the district.
evidence: 8 residential disposal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.8 weekly average (191% spike, z-score 4.04)
First significant spike of this category in recent 90-day period
Timing coincides with potential seasonal waste volume increase or service disruption
reporting_angles: Interview residents in high-complaint blocks to identify what illegal dumping or service gaps they're experiencing
Contact DSNY to confirm whether collection routes or contractor coverage changed this week in Sheepshead Bay/Gravesend

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge Across District
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 12 reports LAST WEEK, a 465% spike over the 2.1 weekly baseline from the prior 8 weeks, indicating a possible coordinated tagging campaign or gang activity.
evidence: 12 graffiti complaints last week vs. 2.1 weekly average (465% spike, z-score 4.73)
Most significant spike in graffiti activity in the 90-day window
High z-score (4.73) indicates statistically anomalous concentration
reporting_angles: Map the 12 graffiti locations to identify whether they cluster geographically or target specific building types
Reach out to NYPD's transit/community safety unit to determine if this is organized crew activity or opportunistic tagging

themes_detail.label: Construction & Plumbing Boom
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints surged to 64 LAST WEEK, a 241% increase over the 18.8 weekly average, coinciding with 540 DOB building permits filed in the last 90 days—suggesting contractor activity is straining district infrastructure.
evidence: 64 construction/plumbing complaints last week vs. 18.8 weekly average (241% spike, z-score 4.76)
540 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (317 alterations, 87 new buildings, 72 alteration COs, 11 demolitions)
3 active ULURP rezonings in pipeline (1417 Avenue U, 2555 Shell Road, 2959 Avenue Y) suggest ongoing development pressure
reporting_angles: Interview residents on blocks with multiple permit filings to document noise, dust, sidewalk obstruction complaints
Cross-reference the 64 construction complaints with specific DOB permit addresses to identify problem contractors or sites

themes_detail.label: Lot & Property Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints spiked dramatically to 3 reports THREE WEEKS AGO (1100% above the 0.2 weekly average), representing one of the highest z-scores in the dataset (6.35), but signal appears to have cooled since—worth verifying if this was acute or ongoing.
evidence: 3 lot condition complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score 6.35, severity high)
Highest percentage spike in the dataset, but occurred 3 weeks ago rather than this week
No recent follow-up data to confirm whether issue persists or resolved
reporting_angles: Identify the specific lots cited in the 3 complaints to determine if they remain vacant, unsafe, or have been remediated
Check HPD records for open violations or SRO (Serious Repair Orders) on these properties

themes_detail.label: Traffic & Dead Animal Pattern
themes_detail.summary: Traffic complaints (6 reports) and dead animal reports (12 complaints) both spiked 3 weeks ago at z-scores above 5.0, but timing lag raises question: investigate whether these are resolved or part of a broader street sanitation / animal control breakdown.
evidence: 12 dead animal complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.8 weekly average (336% spike, z-score 6.25)
6 traffic complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.5 weekly average (300% spike, z-score 5.2)
Both spikes occurred simultaneously 3 weeks ago, suggesting possible common trigger (accident, event, or service lapse)
reporting_angles: Query NYPD crash data and NYC Parks/Animal Care incident logs for same 3-week window to identify any major incidents
Canvass residents on high-traffic streets to determine if congestion or road conditions have improved since the spike
